headline: José Luis Castro: innovation means narrowing the gap between knowledge and patient care
dek: The WHO Special Envoy for Chronic Respiratory Diseases said at "Visionarios 2026" that primary care, earlier diagnosis and access to essential treatments are key to bringing scientific advances to patients.
body:
José Luis Castro, WHO Director-General Special Envoy for Chronic Respiratory Diseases, wrote on LinkedIn about his contribution to "Visionarios 2026", where he said the discussion of innovation also raised a central question: how to bring scientific advances to people who still receive a late diagnosis or lack timely access to the care they need.

Castro said he opened with the story of a man whose COPD was not diagnosed until breathlessness had limited his daily life. He wrote that the case is a reminder that innovation also means shortening the distance between what is known and what actually reaches patients.

To achieve this, Castro said, primary care must be strengthened, diagnoses made earlier, and access to essential treatments guaranteed. He also called for international commitments, such as resolution WHA78.5, to be turned into concrete action in each country. In Spain, he wrote, progress could be made towards an integrated respiratory health strategy with measurable objectives and effective patient participation.

Castro said the event was marked by the tragedy of Urda. He thanked the organisers and participants and remembered the victims and their families. He also thanked Asomega for publishing his reflections and for giving visibility to lung health.
key_quote: la innovación también consiste en acortar la distancia entre lo que sabemos hacer y lo que realmente llega a los pacientes
